description: Galbi, a cornerstone of Korean BBQ, features succulent beef short ribs marinated in a sweet and savory soy-based sauce. These tender ribs are then grilled to smoky perfection, offering an irresistible balance of flavors and textures. It is a truly satisfying dish that brings the vibrant taste of Korea to your table.

instructions.title: Prepare the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Rinse the flanken-cut short ribs thoroughly under cold water to remove any bone fragments. Pat them completely dry with paper towels. You can make a few shallow slits into the meat (not through the bone) to help the marinade penetrate deeper.

instructions.title: Make the Galbi Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl or blender, combine the soy sauce, brown sugar, grated Asian pear, minced garlic, grated ginger, sesame oil, rice wine, and black pepper. Whisk or blend until the sugar is fully dissolved and the mixture is well combined. The Asian pear acts as a natural tenderizer.

instructions.title: Marinate the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Place the prepared short ribs into a large, non-reactive dish or a resealable plastic bag. Pour the marinade over the ribs, ensuring all pieces are fully coated. Cover the dish or seal the bag and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for maximum flavor and tenderness. For best results, marinate for 24 hours.

instructions.title: Prepare for Grilling
instructions.text: Remove the marinated short ribs from the refrigerator at least 30 minutes before cooking to bring them closer to room temperature. This promotes more even cooking. Preheat your grill (charcoal or gas) to medium-high heat. If using a pan, preheat a heavy-bottomed skillet or cast iron pan over medium-high heat.

instructions.title: Grill the Galbi
instructions.text: Lightly oil the grill grates or pan. Place the short ribs on the hot grill or pan, ensuring not to overcrowd. Grill for 3-5 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness. The ribs should have beautiful char marks and be cooked through but still tender. Cook in batches if necessary.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, transfer the grilled Galbi to a platter. Tent loosely with foil and let them rest for 5 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender and juicy ribs. Garnish generously with chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately with rice and various banchan (Korean side dishes).

tips: To achieve authentic tenderness, do not skip the Asian pear in the marinade; its enzymes naturally break down the meat fibers.
For extra depth of flavor, you can toast the sesame seeds lightly before adding them as a garnish.
Leftover Galbi can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheated gently.
